Respiratory Illness Outbreak Disrupts Automotive Industry in British Virgin Islands

ROAD TOWN, British Virgin Islands, June 13 – An outbreak of acute respiratory illness has swept through the automotive sector in the British Virgin Islands, forcing temporary plant closures and severely impacting production, industry officials said Thursday.

China Zenix Auto International Ltd confirmed that more than 40% of its local workforce is currently absent due to illness or quarantine measures. "We have had to suspend operations at our manufacturing facility in Tortola for at least a week," a company spokesperson said. "Our priority is the health of our employees and the community."

The outbreak, which began last week, has primarily affected factory floor workers, according to the BVI Automotive Manufacturers Association. “Production lines have slowed sharply since Monday, with several companies reporting staff shortages of 30% or more,” said the association’s chair, Judith Malone.

Another major employer, Island Motors Group, reported partial shutdowns at two of its sites. “We are coordinating with health authorities to limit the spread and safeguard our teams,” said operations manager Marcus Hill.

Local authorities have issued health advisories and are conducting testing at industrial sites. Public Health Director Dr. Alicia Morgan said: “This is a rapidly evolving situation. We urge all employers to enforce mask mandates, improve ventilation, and encourage symptomatic workers to stay home.”

Industry analysts estimate output from the territory’s automotive sector could fall by 50% this month if the outbreak continues. “Supply chain delays are already being felt,” said analyst Trevor Finch. “Short-term disruptions may persist until the situation stabilizes.”
